items.description:

waterways.

* WHERE...In New Jersey, Gloucester, Camden and Northwestern
Burlington. In Pennsylvania, Delaware, Philadelphia and Lower
Bucks.

* WHEN...From 11 AM this morning to 7 PM EST Friday.

* IMPACTS...At this level, widespread roadway flooding occurs
along tidal waterways. Some roads become impassable. Minor
damage to vulnerable structures may begin to occur.
items.instruction:
A Coastal Flood Advisory means that minor tidal flooding is
expected. Minor tidal flooding often results in some road
closures. Usually, the most vulnerable roadways will flood.

Do not leave your vehicle at a location that is prone to tidal
flooding. Do not drive your vehicle through flood waters. The
water may be deeper than you think it is. You will be putting
yourself in danger and your vehicle may be damaged, leading to
costly repairs.

Visit the National Water Prediction Service at
https://water.noaa.gov/wfo/phi for additional water level and
flood impact information for your local tide gauge.

items.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued November 26 at 4:33AM EST until November 27 at 12:00PM EST by NWS Upton NY
items.areaDesc: Hudson; Eastern Bergen; Eastern Essex; Eastern Union
items.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Warning, 1 1/2 to 2 1/2 ft of
inundation above ground level expected in vulnerable areas
near the waterfront and shoreline. For the Coastal Flood
Advisory, 1 to 1 1/2 feet of inundation above ground level
possible in vulnerable areas near the waterfront and shoreline.

* WHERE...Hudson, Eastern Bergen, Eastern Essex and Eastern
Union Counties.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Warning, from 7 AM today to 6
AM EST Friday. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, from 8 AM to
noon EST Friday.

* COASTAL FLOOD IMPACTS...Widespread minor to moderate flooding
of vulnerable areas near the waterfront and shoreline,
including roads, parking lots, parks, lawns, and homes and
businesses with basements near the waterfront. Numerous road
closures are likely, and vehicles parked in vulnerable areas
near the waterfront will likely become flooded. Flooding will
also extend inland from the waterfront along tidal rivers and
bays, including the tidal portions of the Hackensack River and
Passaic Rivers.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS... While widespread minor to moderate levels
are still forecast to be reached with this morning's high tide,
this evening's high tide now looks to be the higher of the two
by a few tenths. The forecast has been leaned towards a higher
end water level scenario to provide a bit of safety margin.
items.instruction:
Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone property. If
travel is required, do not drive around barricades or through
water of unknown depth.

items.instruction:

levels and take appropriate action to protect life and property.

officials.

deeper than you think it is. You will be putting yourself in
danger and your vehicle may be damaged, leading to costly
repairs.

https://water.noaa.gov/wfo/phi for additional water level and

* WHAT...East winds 20 to 30 mph with gusts 55 to 65 mph expected,
especially in the immediate western slopes of the Green Mountains.

* WHERE...Eastern Rutland County.

* WHEN...From 4 PM this afternoon to 7 AM EST Friday.

* IMPACTS...Damaging winds will likely blow down trees and power
lines. Scattered to numerous power outages are possible. Travel
will be difficult, especially for high profile vehicles.
items.instruction:
Remain in the lower levels of your home during the windstorm, and
avoid windows. Watch for falling debris and tree limbs. Use caution
if you must drive.

People are urged to secure loose objects that could be blown around
or damaged by the wind.

items.headline: Wind Advisory issued November 26 at 1:09PM EST until November 27 at 7:00AM EST by NWS Burlington VT
items.areaDesc: Western Rutland; Eastern Addison
items.description:
* WHAT...East winds 15 to 25 mph with gusts up to 45 mph expected.
Locally stronger gusts up to 55 mph possible near the western
slopes of the Green Mountains and Taconic Highlands.

* WHERE...Eastern Addison and Western Rutland Counties.

* WHEN...From 4 PM this afternoon to 7 AM EST Friday.

* IMPACTS...Gusty winds will blow around unsecured objects. Tree
limbs could be blown down and a few power outages may result.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Surges of wind are expected with a period of
lighter wind in between. Most likely timing will be during the
evening before steady rain arrives, and during the early morning
hours after rain tapers off.
items.instruction:
Winds this strong can make driving difficult, especially for high
profile vehicles. Use extra caution.

Secure outdoor objects.

items.headline: Wind Advisory issued November 26 at 1:09PM EST until November 27 at 7:00AM EST by NWS Burlington VT
items.areaDesc: Southeastern St. Lawrence; Southern Franklin; Western Essex; Orleans; Essex; Lamoille; Eastern Franklin; Eastern Chittenden
items.description:
* WHAT...East winds 10 to 25 mph with gusts up to 45 mph expected.

* WHERE...In New York, Southeastern St. Lawrence, Southern Franklin,
and Western Essex Counties. In Vermont, Essex, Orleans, Eastern
Chittenden, Eastern Franklin, and Lamoille Counties.

* WHEN...From 4 PM this afternoon to 7 AM EST Friday.

* IMPACTS...Gusty winds will blow around unsecured objects. Tree
limbs could be blown down and a few power outages may result.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Strongest winds are most likely after rain
tapers off in the early morning hours. Winds may be light for much
of the event aside from high terrain.
items.instruction:
Winds this strong can make driving difficult, especially for high
profile vehicles. Use extra caution.

Secure outdoor objects.

items.headline: Winter Weather Advisory issued November 26 at 12:53PM EST until November 27 at 7:00AM EST by NWS Albany NY
items.areaDesc: Hamilton; Northern Warren; Bennington; Western Windham
items.description:
* WHAT...Freezing rain expected. Total ice accumulations around one
tenth of an inch.

* WHERE...In New York, Northern Warren and Hamilton Counties. In
Vermont, Bennington and Western Windham Counties.

* WHEN...From 4 PM this afternoon to 7 AM EST Friday.

* IMPACTS...Slick travel conditions are possible. Allow for extra
time and drive carefully.
items.instruction:
Slow down and use caution while traveling. Prepare for possible power
outages. The latest road conditions for the state you are calling
from can be obtained by calling 5 1 1.

Be prepared for slippery roads. Slow down and use caution while
driving. If you are going outside, watch your first few steps taken
on stairs, sidewalks, and driveways. These surfaces could be icy and
slippery, increasing your risk of a fall and injury.

items.headline: High Wind Warning issued November 26 at 12:49PM EST until November 27 at 7:00AM EST by NWS Albany NY
items.areaDesc: Northern Berkshire; Eastern Rensselaer; Bennington
items.description:

* WHERE...In Massachusetts, Northern Berkshire County. In New York,
Eastern Rensselaer County. In Vermont, Bennington County.

* WHEN...Until 7 AM EST Friday.

* IMPACTS...Damaging winds will blow down trees and power lines.
Widespread power outages are expected. Travel will be difficult,
especially for high profile vehicles.
items.instruction:
People are urged to secure loose objects that could be blown around
or damaged by the wind.
